underThree.intent: small parts, craft details, hardware, and close-up product dimensions
tips: For small fit checks, compare both inches and millimeters.
Round only after the final conversion.

threeToSix.intent: phone accessories, hand-sized objects, packaging, and small tools
tips: Check whether the listed size means length, width, or diagonal.
Use centimeters for international product listings.

sevenToTwelve.intent: rulers, tablets, notebooks, product dimensions, and household objects
tips: For displays, remember the inch value is diagonal.
Use the exact centimeter result for specifications.

thirteenToTwentyFour.intent: laptops, monitors, shelves, bags, and medium product dimensions
tips: Screen inches are diagonal, not width.
For furniture or bags, convert each dimension separately.

twentyFiveToSixty.intent: TVs, furniture, room planning, signs, and long product dimensions
tips: Large items may need width, depth, and height converted separately.
Leave extra clearance when converting product fit dimensions.

overSixty.intent: large displays, room measurements, furniture, and clearance planning
tips: Consider meters as well as centimeters for long measurements.
Check packaging dimensions separately from product dimensions.

underFive.intent: small objects, parts, craft spacing, and precise product details
tips: Millimeters can be easier for very small measurements.
Keep extra decimal places for technical work.

fiveToFifteen.intent: phones, small boxes, accessories, and hand-sized objects
tips: Use inches when comparing US product dimensions.
Round to fractions only when a tape measure requires it.

fifteenToThirty.intent: tablets, notebooks, rulers, and medium product dimensions
tips: Check whether the original value is width, height, or diagonal.
Use decimal inches for accurate product listings.

thirtyToOneHundred.intent: screens, furniture, shelves, luggage, and larger product dimensions
tips: Convert length, width, and height separately.
For screens, diagonal size does not equal width.

overOneHundred.intent: furniture, height references, large displays, and room planning
tips: Meters may be clearer for long centimeter values.
Keep the exact centimeter value for forms and specifications.

underFiveFeet.intent: child height records, character profiles, school forms, and metric references
tips: Use centimeters when the form requests metric height.
Keep feet and inches together to avoid losing the remaining inches.

fiveToSixFeet.intent: personal height conversion, fitness profiles, clothing references, travel forms, and ID records
tips: Convert feet to total inches before multiplying by 2.54.
For official forms, use the exact centimeter value or the required rounding rule.

overSixFeet.intent: sports profiles, athlete bios, clearance references, and international height comparison

Use centimeters for international rosters and profiles.
